key_insight: LizTail adds predefined segment-level reconfiguration to a systolic array so one accelerator can both reshape for awkward matrix dimensions and expose more parallelism when workloads are split across independent tasks.
engineering_relevance: This matters for CNN inference and LLM decoding, where fixed arrays waste many PEs on skinny matrices, small batches, and partitioned operators, causing low utilization and repeated folding.
method: Partitions a 128×128 array into 32 reconfigurable 128×4 segments.
Uses limited endpoint connectivity with trimming, 180° turn-back extension, and distributed execution across segments.
Adds segment-aware buffers and differentiated PE datapaths, guided by a hardware-constrained mapper.
evidence_signal: On representative workloads, the design reports geometric-mean speedups of 5.02× for CNNs and 25.67× for LLM decoding over a TPU-like array, with up to 38.23× EDP reduction.
watch_item: The flexibility comes from constrained but still nontrivial interconnect, buffering, and control logic, so area and design complexity must be managed carefully.
paper_title: LizTail: Unifying Shape Adaptation and Spatial Parallelism with Segment-Reconfigurable Systolic Arrays
